items.name: Natural History Museum
items.description: Home to the famous blue whale skeleton 'Hope' and Dippy the Diplodocus cast. Kids love the dinosaur gallery and the interactive Darwin Centre.

items.name: Science Museum
items.description: Interactive exhibits on space, technology, medicine and more. The Wonderlab is perfect for curious kids aged 7 and up.

items.name: ZSL London Zoo
items.description: One of the world's oldest zoos with over 700 species. Kids love the Gorilla Kingdom, Tiger Territory and the new Land of the Lions.

items.name: Hyde Park Playground
items.description: The Diana Memorial Playground is a magical Peter Pan-themed play area with a giant pirate ship. Free entry and perfect for under 12s.

items.name: SEA LIFE London Aquarium
items.description: Over 600 species of sea life including sharks, rays and penguins. The interactive rock pools are a favourite with younger children.

items.name: Museum of London Docklands
items.description: Fascinating journey through London's history from Roman times to the present. The Mudlarks children's gallery is hands-on and educational.

items.name: Kew Gardens
items.description: Stunning botanical gardens with a Treetop Walkway, children's garden and seasonal activities. Beautiful year-round destination for families.

items.name: LEGOLAND Windsor
items.description: The ultimate LEGO experience with over 55 rides and attractions. Miniland features famous London landmarks built entirely from LEGO bricks.

items.name: Legoland Discovery Centre
items.description: Indoor LEGO adventure with rides, 4D cinema, LEGO build zones and a miniature London made entirely from LEGO bricks. Kids go wild.

items.name: V&A Museum of Childhood
items.description: Free museum dedicated to the history of childhood — toys, games, dolls and clothes spanning 400 years. Great rainy day activity.

items.name: Westfield Play Area
items.description: Indoor play zones, soft play and entertainment areas in Europe's largest urban shopping centre. Perfect when weather is bad.

items.name: Richmond Park
items.description: London's largest Royal Park with hundreds of wild deer roaming free. Cycling, picnics, ponds and open space. Kids absolutely love the deer.

items.name: London Eye
items.description: Iconic giant observation wheel on the Thames. Stunning 360° views across London from 135 metres. Kids love the pods and the views.

items.name: Discover Children's Story Centre
items.description: Magical creative play centre inspired by stories and books. Dedicated to children aged 0–11 with interactive storytelling worlds.

items.name: Battersea Park Adventure Playground
items.description: Large adventure playground in beautiful Battersea Park on the Thames. With a children's zoo, boating lake, Go Ape and spectacular sculptures.

items.name: Namco Funscape
items.description: Massive indoor entertainment venue with bowling, bumper cars, arcade games and laser tag. Great for rainy days and birthday parties.

items.name: Tower of London
items.description: Nearly 1000 years of history — crown jewels, Beefeaters, ravens and medieval armour. Kids love the interactive tours and the dark history.

items.name: Natural History Museum Wildlife Garden
items.description: Hidden garden inside the Natural History Museum grounds. Meadows, pond and woodland — a little piece of countryside in central London. Free.

items.name: Gambado Chelsea
items.description: Huge indoor play centre with slides, climbing frames, ball pits and a cafe for parents. Perfect for a rainy day with younger kids.

items.name: Flip Out Trampoline Park
items.description: Huge trampoline park with foam pits, dodgeball courts and climbing walls. Great for energetic kids and teens.

items.name: Little Angel Theatre
items.description: Charming puppet theatre showing magical productions specifically designed for young children. A unique cultural experience.

items.name: Diana Memorial Playground
items.description: Famous pirate ship-themed playground inspired by Peter Pan, with sand pits, teepees and climbing structures. Completely free.

items.name: Bramley's Big Adventure
items.description: Organised chaos beneath the Westway flyover — a giant three-level play frame with slides, ball pools, swings and dens, plus a calmer area for under-fives.

items.name: Oxygen Freejumping at The O2
items.description: More than a trampoline park — interconnected trampolines, ninja-style obstacle courses and climbing walls that keep kids moving the whole visit.

items.name: Clip 'n Climb
items.description: Colourful, safe climbing walls with auto-belay systems — perfect for kids who love a physical challenge, no experience needed.

items.name: Kidspace Croydon
items.description: One of the largest indoor play centres in South London — multi-level play frames, slides, ball pits and dedicated areas for younger children.

items.name: Museum of London Docklands - Mudlarks Gallery
items.description: A brilliant, affordable rainy-day option — the Mudlarks Family Gallery has hands-on climbing, role play and dockside-themed props for under-8s. Timed sessions, book ahead.
items.entryFee: Museum free, Mudlarks Gallery small charge

items.name: RAF Museum London
items.description: A free national museum celebrating the Royal Air Force — real aircraft, interactive exhibits and hands-on activities that fascinate kids of all ages.

items.name: National Maritime Museum
items.description: The world's largest maritime museum, free to enter — inspiring stories of exploration and adventure at sea, great for curious kids.

items.name: Jump London
items.description: A massive 100,000 sq ft multi-activity centre with 12 trampoline zones for jumping, flipping and sliding, plus an on-site go-karting track for older kids and teens.

items.name: ZapSpace Stratford
items.description: A three-storey trampoline park with a dedicated soft play area for toddlers aged 1-4 and a sensory-friendly programme for children with additional needs. Includes an on-site café for parents.

items.name: Gravity Max
items.description: A large-format entertainment venue combining bowling, e-karting, virtual reality and Immersive Gamebox — where the whole wall becomes part of the game. Popular for birthday parties and rainy-day trips.

items.name: Coldharbour Adventure Play Centre
items.description: Indoor and outdoor climbing frames and sports facilities designed for active kids to burn energy at weekends, with structured play sessions supervised by staff.

items.name: Oxygen Freejumping Acton
items.description: A trampoline adventure park with wall-to-wall trampolines, obstacle courses, foam pits, a parkour zone, dodgeball courts and a dedicated toddler area. One of West London's most complete indoor activity venues.

items.name: Flip Out Brent Cross
items.description: A large trampoline park with a dedicated kids' area, battle cannon zone, inflatable obstacle course, donut slide and soft play zone — one of the biggest of its kind in North London.

items.name: Kidzmania
items.description: A soft play centre with a dedicated under-3s area featuring a bouncy castle, ball pool and play cars, plus towers and tunnels for older kids to climb and slide through.

items.name: Kidspace Romford
items.description: A sister site to Kidspace Croydon, with slides, climbing walls, go-karts, mini-golf, ball blasters and UV-lit tunnels across distinctively themed zones. Suitable for anyone under 13.

items.name: Golders Hill Park Adventure Playground
items.description: A free adventure playground next to Hampstead Heath, with climbing structures, a small zoo enclosure and beautiful surrounding parkland — a genuine countryside escape within the city.

items.name: Oxygen at The O2
items.description: More than a trampoline park — interconnected trampolines, ninja-style obstacle courses, climbing walls and high-energy zones, conveniently located inside The O2 entertainment complex.

items.name: ArcelorMittal Orbit Slide
items.description: The UK's tallest and longest tunnel slide, spiralling down from the top of the iconic Orbit sculpture in Olympic Park. A thrilling ride with panoramic London views from the top first.

items.name: AeroPlay at RAF Museum
items.description: An aviation-themed indoor soft play area newly opened inside the free RAF Museum London, designed for younger children with plane-shaped climbing structures and slides.

items.name: Coram's Fields
items.description: A unique children-only park — adults may only enter accompanied by a child under 16. Seven acres with a huge sandpit, paddling pool, city farm with goats, and an adventure playground with a zip wire and tunnel slide.

items.name: Battersea Park Playground
items.description: A colourful, landscape-architect-designed playground with swings, slides, exercise stations and trapeze bars, plus the nearby paid Go Ape treetop course for older kids.

items.name: Victoria Park Playground
items.description: An East London favourite with water fountains and climbing structures set within one of the city's most popular parks — a great combination of playground and open green space.

items.name: Tumbling Bay Playground
items.description: A nature-inspired playground with sand pools, tree houses, rickety bridges and rock scrambles, giving kids space to run freely within the Olympic Park.

items.name: Dulwich Park Playground
items.description: A large, well-equipped playground in leafy South London, part of a beautiful Victorian park with a boating lake and cycling paths nearby.

items.name: Petersham Gate Playground
items.description: A newly refurbished wooden playground inside Richmond Park with a large sand area and a giant seesaw kids run back and forth along — a genuine day out combined with the park's deer.
items.openingHours: Daily, park hours vary by season

items.name: Gymfinity Kids
items.description: Purpose-built gymnastics, ninja and dance clubs with advanced equipment. Weekly classes plus monthly Club Nights on Fridays for extra fun after regular sessions.

items.name: The Little Gym Hampstead
items.description: Structured gymnastics classes for young children building strength, flexibility and confidence in a supportive, non-competitive environment.

items.name: Dakodas Children's Dance & Performing Arts
items.description: A leading dance and performing arts academy across seven London studios, offering acro-gymnastics and musical theatre classes for children aged 18 months to 16 years.

items.name: Stagecoach Theatre Arts
items.description: Weekly drama, dance and singing classes across London, building confidence and performing arts skills through part-time training and regular productions.

items.name: GymLab Stratford
items.description: A Montessori-influenced children's gymnastics centre focused on friendship and personal growth over competition, plus seasonal holiday camps combining ballet, gymnastics and free play.
items.openingHours: Weekly classes; camps during school breaks

items.name: Warner Bros. Studio Tour London
items.description: A family day out through film sets, costumes and production details from the Harry Potter films. The studio is near Watford, outside central London; book ahead.

items.name: Chessington World of Adventures
items.description: A theme park and zoo in southwest Greater London with rides for a range of ages. Check ride height limits and opening dates before travelling.

items.name: Horniman Museum and Gardens
items.description: Explore natural history displays, musical instruments and gardens at this family-friendly Forest Hill museum. Some special attractions need tickets.
items.entryFee: Main museum and gardens free; some attractions ticketed

items.name: London Wetland Centre
items.description: Follow trails through urban wetland habitats and look for birds and other wildlife. A slower-paced outdoor trip for families.

items.name: The Postal Museum and Mail Rail
items.description: Learn how London’s post travelled and ride the underground Mail Rail train. Check ride access and ticket availability with the museum.

items.name: IFS Cloud Cable Car
items.description: Cross the Thames by cable car for aerial views of the peninsula and docks. Check the operator for fares and service updates.

items.name: London Transport Museum
items.description: Explore historic buses, trains and the story of getting around London in the former Covent Garden flower market building.

items.name: Up at The O2
items.description: Take a guided climb over The O2’s roof for skyline views. Children must meet the operator’s age and height requirements.
